title: How can one power be written as a power of a power?
description: Four powers are each written with a power inside brackets in two different ways, by splitting the exponent into two numbers that multiply to it or by rewriting the base. Keeko's doubt is that two plus four gives eight to the power six.
teaching_notes: One idea: a power inside brackets with a power outside has its two small numbers multiplied, so the exponent is split into two numbers that multiply to it. Watch for students who add the two small numbers instead of multiplying them.

source: Write 8 to the power 6, 7 to the power 15, 9 to the power 14
video_script.why: The child can work out a power inside brackets and now goes the other way, writing one power as a power of a power in two ways.
video_script.substitution: The book's own four powers, each split two ways by breaking the exponent into two numbers that multiply to it or by rewriting the base.
video_script.anchor: the four powers on the board, each exponent split into two numbers that multiply to it
video_script.wrong_answer: eight squared, all to the power four
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks eight to the power six is eight squared, all to the power four, because two plus four is six. Four groups of two eights make eight eights, so the exponent is two times four, which is eight.
video_script.payoff_line: Five to the power eight is also five to the power four, all squared

final_answer.value: For example (8²)³ and (2³) to the power 6; (7³) to the power 5 and (7 to the power 5)³; (9²) to the power 7 and (3²) to the power 14; (5²)⁴ and (5⁴)²
final_answer.spoken: for example, eight squared, all cubed, and two cubed, all to the power six; seven cubed, all to the power five, and seven to the power five, all cubed; nine squared, all to the power seven, and three squared, all to the power fourteen; five squared, all to the power four, and five to the power four, all squared

video_script.design: One idea: split the exponent into two numbers that multiply to it. The four powers stay on the board all video; the swapped form of the last power is left open until the answer; one slip at the end.

beats.on_screen: title card, From your book; 8⁶, 7¹⁵, 9¹⁴ and 5⁸ on the board

marks.book: the title card From your book arrives
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside the four powers

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about powers inside brackets.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Eight to the power six and seven to the power fifteen are on the board.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Nine to the power fourteen and five to the power eight are beside them.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we write each one inside brackets in two different ways?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.rule: (8²)³ is opened into three groups of 8², making six 8s

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Eight squared, all cubed, is three groups of eight squared.
That is six eights, because two times three is six.
<bookmark mark='split'/>We split the exponent into two numbers that multiply to it.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eight to the power six and seven to the power fifteen.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Also nine to the power fourteen and five to the power eight.

beats.on_screen: To find: each power inside brackets in two ways
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each power inside brackets in two different ways.

marks.one: 6 is split as 2 × 3 and (8²)³ is written
marks.base: 8 is rewritten as 2³ and (2³)⁶ is written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, six is two times three.
Eight to the power six is then eight squared, all cubed.
<bookmark mark='base'/>Eight is also two cubed.
That makes eight to the power six equal to two cubed, all to the power six.

marks.two: 15 is split as 3 × 5 and (7³)⁵ is written
marks.swap: 3 and 5 are swapped and (7⁵)³ is written

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, fifteen is three times five.
Seven to the power fifteen is seven cubed, all to the power five.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>Swap the two numbers, and it is seven to the power five, all cubed.

marks.three: 14 is split as 2 × 7 and (9²)⁷ is written
marks.base: 9 is rewritten as 3² and (3²)¹⁴ is written

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, fourteen is two times seven.
Nine to the power fourteen is nine squared, all to the power seven.
<bookmark mark='base'/>Nine is also three squared.
That makes nine to the power fourteen equal to three squared, all to the power fourteen.

marks.four: 8 is split as 2 × 4 and (5²)⁴ is written
marks.swap: 2 and 4 are swapped and the new form is left open

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, eight is two times four.
Five to the power eight is five squared, all to the power four.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>Swapping the two numbers is left to find.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>Eight to the power six is eight squared, all cubed.
It is also two cubed, all to the power six.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Seven to the power fifteen is seven cubed, all to the power five.
It is also seven to the power five, all cubed.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Nine to the power fourteen is nine squared, all to the power seven.
It is also three squared, all to the power fourteen.
<bookmark mark='a4'/>Five to the power eight is five squared, all to the power four.
Five to the power eight is also five to the power four, all squared.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the four powers
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: (8²)⁴ = 8⁶ appears with 2 + 4 = 6, then is crossed out; the eights are counted: 2 × 4 = 8

marks.count: 8⁶ is crossed out and the eights in four groups of two are counted one by one up to 8

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks eight to the power six is eight squared, all to the power four.
Two plus four is six, Keeko says.
<bookmark mark='count'/>But eight squared, all to the power four, is four groups of two eights.
That is eight eights, not six.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The exponent is two times four, which is eight.
